_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 natively to contract v3, mirroring the Dubai v3 fleet-investors gold master per the international addendum (RSG run — RESORT-TRANSFER revenue shape). Sources: red-sea-global/NODES + REVENUE-INPUTS + FARE-BENCHMARKS + CREW-COST-BENCHMARKS + DEMAND-POOLS + AUTHORITY-MAP + SPEED-RULES (all -RED-SEA-GLOBAL.md). CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — equity/fundraise/counterparty content firewalls apply in full. THIS IS THE ONE MARKET WHERE THE UTILIZATION STACK IS RE-KEYED: no commuter seat bundles exist — L1 is contracted resort guest transfers, L2 scheduled inter-island/experience seats, L3 private charters. Tiers are keyed to hotel-opening STATUS, never years. U1 sponsorship and U2 resort-resupply cargo are unsourced in this market and therefore render unpriced, upside-only, never summed — the upside scenario contains NO priced upside lines (deviation from the Dubai gold master, where both were priced). Berthing and insurance are excluded and disclosed (marina tariffs unpublished). All scenario figures script-verified to $0 diff before writing. Demand pools are sourced key counts / occupancy signals / visitor flows, labeled indicative. No phasing or fleet-count section: no sourced RSG fleet plan exists in the research set, so none renders.

fn1.text: Pricing is positioned against the transfer market the destination already operates: a published resort transfer fee near SAR 1,370 round trip (about $183 one-way), seaplane transfers reported near $230–390 one-way, Maldives island-transfer comparables, and the regional day-charter market — trade-published figures used as anchors, not quotes.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential across these waters — sourced key counts, occupancy signals and visitor flows, not commitments or commercial relationships with any developer or resort brand.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship, overnight resupply, staff shuttles and zone relief — are unpriced where unsourced and never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times assume 25 knots in open lagoon water on marked transfer routes and 8 knots within half a nautical mile of every landing and across flagged conservation areas — a stated planning assumption, not a published rule. Distances are coordinate-derived pending a pinning pass.

fn5.text: Guest-transfer pricing is a derived band, not a quote: $140–200 per guest one-way (SAR 525–750), anchored at the level of today's published resort transfer fee and below the seaplane floor. Pending confirmation.

fn6.text: Crew costs use a Saudi-adapted method: national maritime wage bands for a two-person crew (captain + deckhand), explicitly stated burden, and an explicit remote-site uplift for housing, rotation travel and retention. The model uses $42 per hour loaded — the mid benchmark rounded up as a buffer.

fn7.text: Scenario quantities derive from a stated chain: open keys × occupancy × 1.9 guests per room ÷ 3.5-night stays × two transfer legs, less a 30–40% seaplane share — every link a stated assumption, with this vessel taking a deliberately thin share of the resulting flow.

fn8.text: The conservative case assumes today's open hotels only and deliberately thin shares of every layer, and pays back in about 9.9 years — shown as the floor, not a financing case.

fn9.text: A 12-month operating year on warm, sheltered water. June–September heat shifts midday leisure sailings toward morning and evening slots; arrival and departure transfers run unaffected in a climate-controlled cabin. Scenario counts are annual monthly averages with that shape absorbed.

fn10.text: Energy is priced at the national commercial electricity tariff — about $0.085 per kWh. The destination itself runs on a 100% solar, off-grid microgrid, so actual charging economics are a counterparty conversation; the national tariff stands in as a stated proxy assumption.

fn11.text: All figures are US dollars. Local benchmarks are cited in Saudi riyals and convert at the pegged rate of 3.75 riyals per dollar.

fn12.text: Tiers are keyed to hotel-opening status, never to years: conservative is today's open hotels only; mid is the destination's published current build-out complete; upside is the fuller published vision.

fn13.text: Berthing and insurance are excluded from operating cost and payback: marina tariffs at Shura and Triple Bay are unpublished and no local insurance quote exists. Both are counterparty terms; adding them will lengthen paybacks.

fn14.text: Laheq Island's marina is announced by the developer. It renders as roadmap reach only, with no demand modeled on it.

network.title: The network
network.note: The Al Wajh lagoon and Triple Bay — Turtle Bay to the Ummahat islands in about 44 minutes, vs about 90 minutes door-to-door today.
network._internal: Geometry source: NODES-RED-SEA-GLOBAL.md. ZERO Atlas corridor bindings — the partner census confirms n_sourced = 0 for this geography, and the sealed sets were never used (fail-closed per the international addendum). All legs are coordinate-derived (haversine × 1.15 routing factor, ±15%), times at 25 kn + 6 min dwell with an 8 kn harbor/reef regime assumption. Line working labels (RSG-1/2/3) are NOT sealed route_ids — no IDs invented. Stops (6 operating landings): Turtle Bay Jetty (A2), Shura Island Marina (A1, hub), St. Regis jetty + Nujuma jetty (A3 Ummahat — coords LOW precision), Shebara jetty (A4), Triple Bay Marina / AMAALA Yacht Club (B1, hub). RSG-1 = A2↔A1 (~13 min) ↔ A3 (~37 min; through ~44 min vs ~90 min car+vessel today). RSG-2 = A1↔A4 (~31 min; operating variant A2↔A4 ~34 min, today's transfer corridor). RSG-3 = B1-anchored local loop (1–2 nm hops; resort frontage calls fail closed until jetties verified — B2). Roadmap (never rendered as active): Laheq infill (announced, fn14), RSG-T Thuwal (C1 KAUST North Marina ↔ C2 retreat, ~25–37 min foiling, island coords unsourced), Al Wajh / Umluj gateways (no verified tourist landings), Triple Bay↔Shura inter-destination 79.3 nm direct — beyond the N45/N30 electric envelope, long-range platform class only, NEVER in vessel economics. Grok seal note: this geometry is NEW — a coordinate-pinning pass to jetty precision is required before sealing (A3/A6/C2 flagged LOW/unsourced). No launch dates anywhere.

_internal.sources: REVENUE-INPUTS-RED-SEA-GLOBAL.md (layers, occupancy chain, cost inputs — no final P&L existed there; assembled here). Prices: FARE-BENCHMARKS §5 DERIVED bands. Crew: CREW-COST-BENCHMARKS (SAUDI-ADAPTED + REMOTE uplift; LOW $23.9 / MID $41.9; model $42/hr). Energy: SERA/SEC proxy $0.0853/kWh × 4.1 kWh/nm = $0.34973/nm.

opex_basis.crew: Per-scenario activity hours × $42/hr: 198/245/300 hrs = $8,316/$10,290/$12,600; rendered as the band. Hours DERIVED from the 16-h service-day duty cycle at thin/mid/full activity (program precedent).
opex_basis.energy: Per-scenario distance 2,400/3,300/4,500 nm/mo (80/110/150 nm/day vs the NODES 120–180 nm/day duty band — conservative below band deliberately) × $0.34973/nm = $839/$1,154/$1,574.
opex_basis.maintenance: $82.5K/yr = $6,875/mo, program-consistent N45 figure, flat across scenarios (instruction canon for this market).
opex_basis.berthing_insurance: EXCLUDED + disclosed (fn13): Shura (115–118 berths) and Triple Bay (10-ha) marinas exist [PRIMARY] but tariffs unpublished; no UAE-style placeholder used per instruction. Counterparty term.

L2: 120/240/360 seats/mo (4/8/12 per day) vs the 0.3–0.8 trips/guest-day discretionary pool. L3: 8/14/20 charter-hrs/mo vs a 1–3 charters/vessel-day in-season potential. navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 20 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the water for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional hulls. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.
